q: (_with the_ Train of Suppliants _grouped before an altar_)

l: The Seven Plays in English Verse
s: Theban citizens suffers from the plague afflicting Thebes (with widespread death and infertility)
q: Our city is tempest tost, and all too weak To lift above the waves her weary prow That plunges in a rude and ravenous sea. Earth's buds are nipped, withering the germs within, Our cattle lose their increase, and our wives Have fruitless travail; and that scourge from Heaven, The fiery Pestilence abhorred of men, Descending on our people with dire stroke Lays waste the Home of Cadmus

l: The Seven Plays in English Verse
s: Thebes is ruled by Oedipus (prosperously before the plague)
q: He reigned nobly and prosperously

l: The Seven Plays in English Verse
s: Thebes is the home of Sphinx (during her ravages)
q: He went onward till he came near Thebes, where the Sphinx was making havoc of the noblest citizens

l: The Seven Plays in English Verse
s: Sphinx is a songstress (hateful and destructive)
q: Thou, in thy coming to this Theban land, Didst take away the hateful tax we paid To that stern songstress
